source.title: Attention Output SAEs Improve Circuit Analysis

record.tranche_reason: Applies sparse-autoencoder feature analysis to GPT-2 Small and reports results bearing on whether dictionary features in a language model capture causally relevant information and preserve task behavior.
record.gate_note: The post mentions the superposition hypothesis as background but does not test toy-model superposition geometry, feature-capacity competition, or one-dimensional directions. Rows cover its SAE feature and reconstruction results; the positional-signal noising experiments do not measure a claim version and are omitted.
record.test_reason: The post applies attention-output and residual SAEs to GPT-2 Small. It states that it aims to test whether SAE features are 'the real variables of the model's computation'. It reports whether SAE reconstructions preserve IOI behaviour layer by layer (V5 completeness), and whether sparse SAE features are causally relevant (V4). It is more than tool use (T4) because sufficiency and causal relevance of the features are the explicit object of evaluation.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that attention-output SAEs gave novel IOI insights: the positional signal is whether the duplicate name is before or after ' and'. They also enabled recursive DFA. However, several layers (0 and later) have significant reconstruction error, so SAEs are not yet a silver bullet for end-to-end circuit analysis.
record.recipe_differences: The study does not reproduce the Toy Models of Superposition method; it uses attention-output and residual-stream SAEs for GPT-2 Small circuit analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies by layer and head-group cross-section; the feature findings also differ between ABBA and BABA prompt templates.
record.problems: The authors report significant reconstruction error in several layers and describe the causal feature investigations as relatively shallow. Numerical results and uncertainty estimates are not provided for many layer and cross-section findings; only 100 prompts are specified for the feature and QK analyses.
record.rows_left_out: The post also reports zero-ablating the SAE error term with a minor effect, but gives no numerical result. It describes noising experiments on induction-layer outputs and recursive-DFA examples, which do not measure the SAE-feature recovery or completeness named by these claim versions.

untested.parts: All of it: no toy models, geometry or sparsity transition.
All of it: no neuron-level capacity analysis.
Whether features are spread across many neurons.
Stability and canonicality of SAE features across seeds or sizes. Completeness is tested only in IOI and only for attention outputs.
All of it: no test of feature dimensionality.

missing.what: Non-SAE noising experiments validating the SAE-derived hypothesis: ~93% of logit diff recovered when 'and'-relative position is preserved, ~43% when ' and' is replaced by ' alongside'. This is evidence that the recovered features track real model variables.
RDFA 'Dave' example where the resid_pre SAE error term dominates the attribution, a qualitative sign of incompleteness at layer 10.
missing.locator: Example: Retrieving "Dave" using recursive attention attribution

record.verdict_notes: An Alignment Forum post, not peer reviewed. Most layer results are reported only qualitatively from figures, with no numbers in the text. V4 and V5 are split: causal-feature rows support recoverable sparse features (V4). Reconstruction-sufficiency rows bear on completeness (V5) and vary by layer. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, overlap geometry, and sparsity-dependent transitions.
Neuron polysemanticity and competition for representational capacity.
The claim about features spread across many neurons is not tested; only SAE-recovered features are examined.

Stability and canonicality of SAE features are not tested. The post evaluates reconstruction and task-level usefulness for selected layers and circuits, not whether SAE features are complete units of the model in general.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional.
